memories.content: Is a platform engineer at a fintech company working primarily in Go and Python. Builds event-driven microservices.
Has about 8 years of experience in distributed systems and backend engineering. Previously worked at a cloud infrastructure startup.
Prefers Go for performance-critical services and Python for data pipelines and scripting.
Uses Kubernetes, Argo CD, and Temporal in production. Strong opinions about service mesh design.
Currently migrating their team's architecture from synchronous REST to event-driven patterns using Kafka.
Is passionate about observability — uses Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and is adding distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry and Tempo.
Strong believer in schema-first API design using Protocol Buffers and gRPC for internal services.
Read Designing Data-Intensive Applications by Kleppmann and considers it the best technical book they've encountered.
Is an avid sourdough baker. Maintains an active starter and bakes 2-3 loaves per week.
Built a proofing box using a seedling heat mat and Inkbird temperature controller for consistent fermentation.
Prefers a cold retard baking schedule that fits around their work schedule — mix in the evening, fridge overnight, bake in the morning.
Runs their home automation on Home Assistant with Zigbee2MQTT and ESPHome sensors, all communicating over MQTT.
Has approximately 30 ESPHome sensor nodes throughout their house monitoring temperature, humidity, motion, and door states.
Recently migrated smart home devices from WiFi to Zigbee for better reliability and local-only control.
Is building a whole-house energy monitoring system using SCT-013 CT clamps, ADS1115 ADCs, and ESPHome.
Signed up for a 50K trail race in the Cascades with 6,500 feet of elevation gain. Training with stair repeats and weekend trail runs.
Runs 30-40 miles per week, transitioning from road to trail training for the ultramarathon.
Uses systems thinking analogies for everything — baking, running, home automation. Frequently draws parallels between engineering and other domains.
Has a distinctive writing style: uses em-dashes, starts thoughts with 'the thing is' or 'fundamentally', and is concise but precise.
Is mentoring a junior developer on the team, focusing on teaching clean code and function extraction through pairing sessions.
Believes in two-tier on-call alerting: page-worthy (customer-impacting, immediate action) and ticket-worthy (next business day).
Had a P1 incident caused by a config change that bypassed canary deployment checks. Now advocates for config changes going through the same canary process as code changes.
Is evaluating Temporal as a replacement for their current workflow system built from cron jobs, SQS, and DynamoDB.
Building a CLI tool in Go (using Cobra and Charm) to manage sourdough baking schedules with temperature-dependent fermentation calculations.
Redesigned their home network with VLANs using OPNsense — separate trusted, IoT, and guest networks with explicit firewall rules between them.
Prefers to reason about systems in terms of feedback loops: observe, measure, adjust. Applies this to engineering, baking, and training.
Lives in the Pacific Northwest. Kitchen temperature drops to 66°F in fall, affecting starter and fermentation timing.
Uses PgBouncer for Postgres connection pooling in transaction mode to handle connection oversubscription during peak traffic.
Proposed replacing the team's custom service discovery with Consul and using Consul Connect for service mesh with mTLS.
Prefers sourdough at 75% hydration with bread flour. Working on improving crumb openness through longer autolyse and extended bulk fermentation.
Uses the principle 'change one variable at a time' in both debugging and baking experiments.
Ran a controlled experiment baking three loaves at different temperatures (72°F, 78°F, 85°F) with blind taste testing.
Makes pizza dough using sourdough discard at 68% hydration, cold-fermented for 48 hours, baked on a steel at 550°F.
Spouse is tolerant of the engineering approach to baking but occasionally points out the over-engineering.
Proposed implementing rate limiting using token bucket algorithm in Envoy with tiered limits per API key.
Experienced a retry storm from a partner integration that sent 50K requests per second. Uses this as a teaching example for backpressure design.
Values the principle 'guardrails over guidelines' — systems should enforce constraints rather than relying on humans to remember them.
Favorite technical concept: 'a log is the fundamental data structure — tables are just materialized views of a log.'
Plans to do a team book club reading DDIA one chapter per week.
Next technical book on the reading list is Database Internals by Petrov.
Thinks about ESPHome sensor nodes as microservices: single responsibility, well-defined MQTT interface, independently deployable via OTA.
Uses Grafana for both work dashboards and home energy monitoring visualizations.
Standard error handling pattern: machine-readable code, human-readable message, wrappable cause chain that serializes to JSON.
Running OPNsense with Suricata IDS/IPS on a fanless PC as their home firewall.
Has a Sonoff Zigbee coordinator running Zigbee2MQTT on a Raspberry Pi alongside Home Assistant.
Trains for the 50K by doing stair repeats (10x8 floors) at a parking garage near work.
Believes in the run-hike strategy for ultramarathons: optimize for total time, not per-mile pace.
Describes their engineering philosophy as: 'the system should make it hard to introduce the same class of failure twice.'
Uses Argo CD for GitOps-style deployments including monitoring alerting rules.
Working on standardizing Go error handling across all services with a shared error package.
Has three kids. Spouse and neighbors participate as blind taste testers for baking experiments.
Kitchen is equipped with a baking steel, digital scale, and proofing box. Takes cross-section photos of every loaf for crumb analysis.
Stores bake session data in a local SQLite database through their custom CLI tool to track results over time.
Describes circuit breakers as needing backpressure in the half-open state: exponential ramp-up, not instant close.
Compares Zigbee routers to Envoy sidecars in a service mesh — each mains-powered device routes messages for battery-powered end devices.
Uses the phrase 'same principle as' frequently when drawing analogies between different domains.
Prefers phased migrations: run new and old systems in parallel, migrate incrementally, then decommission. Calls it 'blue-green at the infrastructure level.'
Thinks about baking as debugging: 'the crumb doesn't lie' — outcome data tells the truth regardless of what you thought you did.
Is reading Neurofeedback literature for personal interest, particularly around focus and creativity.
Has a strong preference for local-first tools and privacy: runs Home Assistant locally, avoids cloud IoT, uses OPNsense instead of consumer routers.
Listens to technical podcasts during trail runs. Favorites include Software Engineering Daily and Oxide and Friends.
Uses SQLite for personal projects and ClickHouse for analytics workloads at work.
Applies the SRE book's framework for determining page-worthy alerts: 'what action do I need to take right now that can't wait 8 hours?'
Teaches junior developers using the Socratic method — asks questions rather than prescribing solutions.
Motto for code review: 'green tests first, then refactor' — get it working, then make it clean.
Uses BME280 sensors for temperature and humidity in all ESPHome nodes.
Has an automation that alerts if the garage door is open for more than 30 minutes.
Considers the sourdough autolyse analogous to a warm-up phase in distributed systems — preparation that improves the main operation.
Works remotely. Daily standup is at 8:30am which constrains baking schedules.
Has completed the Designing Data-Intensive Applications book club with the team and is considering Database Internals as the next one.
